_comment: A Pterodactyl egg for one dot-server. Import under Nests > a nest > Import Egg. Every setting is an environment variable because ./server takes all of them that way -- see deploy/env.example. GAMES is the one to understand first: a game is a signed pack on the content origin plus a game.yml that says how to start it, and this fetches both at startup, so the install below carries no game content and a server offers exactly what its panel says. rcon_password is deliberately NOT a variable here: it is a secret, and Pterodactyl both displays variables in the panel and puts them in the container environment, where any process in the container can read them. It goes in cfg/rcon.yml, which is a file with a mode on it. The Godot runtime is not a variable either, and for a different reason: it is pinned with its checksum in tools/fetch-godot.sh, so it travels with DEPLOY_BRANCH rather than being restated here where it would drift.
name: dot-server
author: contact@moddingcommunity.com
description: A dot-server that installs the games it is told to run. GAMES is a comma-separated list, fetched from the content origin at startup -- descriptors and signed packs alike -- so this ships no game and a new one needs no new build. TMC_GAME picks which of them boots, and it can be changed live over RCON without a restart.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Installs a dot-server into /mnt/server.
set -euo pipefail

apt-get update -qq
# python3 is NOT optional, and nothing fails without it. setup.sh generates
# cfg/content.json with it -- the file that says which signing keys this server
# trusts -- and the step is guarded by `command -v python3`, so a missing
# interpreter SKIPS SILENTLY. DotCloudClient then starts with
# require_signed_manifests and no keys, and every pack the server is told to fetch
# fails with "no trusted_keys are configured": an install that looks clean and a
# server that cannot download a single map.
apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends \
    git curl unzip ca-certificates python3 >/dev/null

mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server

# --- the server --------------------------------------------------------------
# A shallow clone: the history of this repository is of no use on a game box and
# is most of the download.
REPO="${DEPLOY_REPO:-https://github.com/modcommunity/dot-server-deploy.git}"
BRANCH="${DEPLOY_BRANCH:-main}"

if [ -d .git ]; then
    echo "[install] updating an existing checkout"
    git fetch --depth 1 origin "$BRANCH"
    git reset --hard "origin/$BRANCH"
else
    echo "[install] cloning $REPO ($BRANCH)"
    git clone --depth 1 --branch "$BRANCH" "$REPO" /tmp/deploy
    # Copied rather than cloned in place: /mnt/server is not always empty by the
    # time this runs, and git clone refuses that.
    cp -a /tmp/deploy/. /mnt/server/
    rm -rf /tmp/deploy
fi

# --- the runtime, and why it is not fetched here ------------------------------
# It used to be: a curl of the engine's release zip straight into .runtime/, with
# GODOT_VERSION as a panel variable. Both halves of that were wrong.
#
#   * It was UNVERIFIED. tools/fetch-godot.sh in the checkout pins one version
#     against a sha512 committed to git rather than read from beside the binary,
#     and setup.sh already calls it when the box has no Godot. An egg that
#     downloads its own is thirty lines of curl standing in for that.
#   * It was a SECOND COPY OF THE PINNED VERSION. The panel default and
#     fetch-godot.sh's `GODOT_VERSION` had to be changed together, and the one
#     nobody remembers is the panel -- so the week the engine moves, the egg
#     quietly keeps installing the old runtime against new code. The version
#     belongs to the checkout, and the checkout is cloned above, so pointing
#     DEPLOY_BRANCH at a branch is now the whole of choosing a runtime.
#
# TMC_GODOT_CACHE puts it on the server volume instead of the install container's
# $HOME, which does not survive. setup.sh reads the same variable when it looks
# for a runtime, so a reinstall re-uses this rather than downloading 100 MB again.
export TMC_GODOT_CACHE="/mnt/server/.runtime"

# --- vendor, and write ./server ----------------------------------------------
# No --yes: every question setup.sh asks is inside --full, and this is not that.
# A plain run takes defaults for all of it and never reads stdin.
chmod +x setup.sh
./setup.sh

# --- the games, and the ones this server is not for --------------------------
#
# This repository carries a `game.yml` for every game in the catalogue, because it is
# where they are authored and published from. A SERVER does not want ten of them: the
# panel says which games this box is for, and a server that offers seven more than its
# panel does is a server whose vote menu and whose description disagree.
#
# So the ones nobody asked for are removed here, and they are removable precisely because
# nothing is lost by it -- `./server install-games` fetches any of them back from the
# content origin, descriptor and pack, the moment an id is added to GAMES. `global/` and
# `avatars/` are not games and every game loads them.
#
# Empty GAMES keeps all of them, which is the development case and the right meaning of
# "I did not say".
if [ -n "${TMC_GAMES:-}" ]; then
    for dir in content/*/; do
        id="$(basename "$dir")"

        # A directory with no game.yml is not a game: `global/` is loaded by every one of
        # them and `avatars/` is where a game finds cosmetic parts. Neither is removable.
        [ -f "$dir/game.yml" ] || continue

        # `case` rather than `[ ... ] && continue`, and that is not style: this script runs
        # under `set -e`, where a test that is FALSE ends an && list with status 1 and
        # takes the whole installation down with it. The first game that is not in the
        # list would have failed the install.
        case ",${TMC_GAMES}," in
            *",${id},"*) continue ;;
        esac

        echo "[install] not for this server: $id"
        rm -rf "$dir"
    done

    # And fetch what IS wanted, so the first boot is a boot rather than a download.
    # Never fatal: the origin being unreachable at install time is a slow first start,
    # not a failed installation -- and a panel that reports a failed install for a
    # reason outside the box is a panel people learn to reinstall from twice.
    ./server install-games || echo "[install] games will be fetched at startup instead"
fi

echo
echo "[install] done. cfg/ holds the YAML; put rcon_password in cfg/rcon.yml."

variables.name: Games
variables.description: The games this server installs and offers, comma-separated. Fetched from the content origin the first time they are asked for -- descriptor and pack -- and then started from the disk. Anything else already in content/ is not offered. Leave it empty to offer everything the install brought, which is what a development box wants and not what a panel does. TMC_GAME must name one of these. Known ids: g2gfast (bhop/surf timer), arena (deathmatch), playground (sandbox), lobby, buses (asymmetric), smash, and hungry_classic / hungry_frenzy / hungry_gauntlet / hungry_warrens, which are four modes over one pack.

variables.name: Game
variables.description: Which of GAMES boots. It has to be one of them -- a game that is not installed is reported at startup and the server comes up on whatever else it has, rather than refusing to start. Changeable live over RCON with `changelevel`.

variables.name: Content origin
variables.description: Where games are installed from, comma-separated for mirrors, tried in order. The default is the public origin. A LAN or an air-gapped deployment points this at its own copy; the clients that connect are told the same address, so they download the game from wherever this says rather than from somewhere a second setting mentions.

variables.name: Unlisted games
variables.description: What happens to a game that is installed and is no longer in GAMES. hide: left on the disk and not offered -- putting the id back costs no download. remove: deleted, but only games this server installed itself; anything hand-authored under content/ is never touched. keep: left on the disk AND still offered, which is how a server behaved before GAMES existed.

variables.name: Port
variables.description: The game port. RCON is always this plus one, so two servers a single port apart collide on RCON and nowhere else -- leave a gap of at least 2.

variables.name: Bind address
variables.description: Interface to bind. 0.0.0.0 is every one, which is what a container wants.

variables.name: Server name
variables.description: Shown in listings and in the browser client.

variables.name: Deploy repository
variables.description: Where the server is cloned from at install.

variables.name: Deploy branch
variables.description: Branch to check out at install. This also chooses the Godot runtime: the pinned version and its checksum live in tools/fetch-godot.sh, in the checkout.

variables.name: Verbose logging
variables.description: Set to 1 for debug logging. Empty for normal.
